Subject: Greenbank: HSM requirement + SLA targets for private VPC pilot

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call this morning. A couple of follow-ups from our security and cloud teams:

1) Our compliance team has requested confirmation that any private VPC deployment can integrate with our HSM (Thales) for key wrapping. Is there an established integration path or documented KMS adapter for on-prem HSMs?

2) SLA expectations — we need to understand the realistic P99 latency targets for inference versus what Redwood can commit for a private (VPC/on-prem) pilot. Greenbank requires a written target to use in our procurement packet.

3) Audit evidence — please share any documentation you have that maps your runtime telemetry and audit logs to SOC 2 controls (or provide an inbound checklist).

We attached an outline of our audit scope for reference (GB-Audit-Requirements.pdf). If Redwood needs to propose exception paths (e.g., managed KMS proxy vs. direct HSM peering), outline them along with staffing/ops assumptions.

Can you please loop in the relevant folks on your side for architecture and resourcing? We are aiming to finalize vendor acceptance criteria by Jun 25.

Regards,

Folks — forwarding Greenbank's audit scope and questions. Short summary and proposed decision lanes below.

Summary of asks from Greenbank:
- Direct HSM integration (Thales) or an acceptable exception path;
- Written SLA / P99 latency targets for pilot;
- Audit evidence mapping to SOC2 controls.

Proposed decision lanes (need engineering + product sign-off):
A) Native KMS integration: build a connector that routes key-wrap requests to customer HSM over a secure peering (requires network design + 1 engineer to implement prototype).
B) Managed KMS proxy: Redwood operates a local KMS proxy inside customer VPC that exchanges wrapped keys with customer HSM on a scheduled sync/peering (less intrusive but requires contract language and additional logging).
C) Exception lane: allow Redwood-managed KMS with strict KMS key lifecycle controls + short retention and white-glove audit support (fastest delivery but higher compliance friction).

Immediate asks from product/eng:
- Karthik: quick feasibility on lane A vs B (network footprint, latency impact, security boundary).
- Rishi: sample SLA language we can offer for a pilot (P50/P90/P99, availability target for hosted agent within customer's VPC).
- Marissa: commercial implications and whether pilot can be scoped to existing committed capacity or we need a dedicated commit.

I attached a rough SOW template for the pilot (pilot-sow-draft.docx) to help frame scope and staffing.

Target: align on a recommended lane by EOD Wed Jun 20 so I can get back to Greenbank before their procurement freeze.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Greenbank: HSM requirement + SLA targets for private VPC pilot

Quick architectural readout — my preliminary notes:

- Lane A (native HSM peering): feasible but non-trivial. We'd need a lightweight KMS adapter inside the customer's VPC that can talk to Thales over their private network. Latency: expect +10-40ms per crypto operation depending on network path; must account for batching strategies to amortize cost.

- Lane B (managed KMS proxy): lower customer ops burden but we still need a controlled network tunnel and documented key-wrapping flow. Major advantage: we can keep runtime unchanged and just intercept wrap/unwrap.

- Key points to validate with Greenbank: whether they accept asynchronous key-wrapping for non-critical tokens and whether HSM calls can be elided for cached session keys.

Resourcing ask: to prototype lane A (end-to-end peering + e2e test harness) we will need 2 infra engineers for 4 weeks and 1 security engineer part-time (for review and threat model). For lane B prototype (KMS proxy), 1 infra + 1 product engineer for 3 weeks.

Operational considerations:
- IP allowlist & firewall rules (customer must open specific ports/paths).
- Audit log retention: if Greenbank requires 7 years, that implies additional storage and longer retention in our private telemetry sink — need finance estimate.
- HSM credentials rotation — define a clear rotation playbook and recovery path in the SOW.

I'll prepare a concise tech appendix for Hannah to share with Greenbank by Tue EOD.

-Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Thanks for the clear lanes. Commercial notes:

- Pilot funding: we should propose a short 8-week paid pilot with a capped not-to-exceed fee that covers the 2 infra engineers + security time Karthik mentioned plus a modest seat of dedicated capacity. I attached a quick cost sketch.

- Commitment reuse: Greenbank has an existing RFP for hosted capacity; suggest we offer a credit if they convert to a 12-month dedicated commit after pilot. That will make the procurement team happier.

- SLA language: avoid hard P99 numbers until we have telemetry from the prototype; offer a target range (e.g., P99 <= 650ms for typical 512-token requests) with a carve-out for crypto ops when they require synchronous HSM hits. Rishi — can you draft that wording?

Subject: Re: Greenbank: HSM requirement + SLA targets for private VPC pilot

Samir — thanks for the detailed scope. We're aligned to move forward with a narrow, paid pilot that gives both sides the engineering visibility we need. Proposed next steps:

1) Pilot lane: start with Lane B (managed KMS proxy) as a pragmatic path to reduce footprint and accelerate delivery. We will prototype the KMS proxy and demonstrate audit telemetry. If Greenbank requires direct peering after the pilot, we can escalate to Lane A.

2) Timeline & staffing: 8-week pilot; Redwood will provide 1 infra engineer + 1 product engineer (proxy build) and 1 SRE for runbook/handoff. If Greenbank prefers Lane A from the outset, scope changes to 2 infra + 1 security for the prototype.

3) SLA/latency: We'll offer target ranges for pilot: P50 ~ 40–60ms; P90 ~ 120–200ms; P99 <= 650ms for 512-token workloads under normal load with caveat that synchronous HSM operations may add variable latency. We will include instrumentation in the pilot SOW for per-token breakdown.

4) Audit evidence: we'll provide a mapping document to SOC2 controls and white-glove log export for the pilot period.

Commercial: Marissa has provided a cost sketch; we'll propose a convert-to-commit credit in the SOW to ease procurement.

Action items:
- Hannah: send this proposal to Samir and request a confirmation of lane (B preferred) by Thu Jun 22.
- Karthik: tech appendix and test plan for Tue Jun 20.
- Rishi: draft pilot SLA language by Wed Jun 21.
- Marissa: finalize pilot cost and credit structure by Wed Jun 21.

If Greenbank confirms lane B, we'll issue an updated pilot SOW and an attached short appendix for the procurement packet.

Best,
Hannah
